tickets.title: Repair unattended/07: permission proof narrows unproven forms to main instead of approving them
tickets.live_try: In a scratch herdr pane bound to a synthetic job, show Claude Bash prompts for (a) `S=<scratchpad>; rm -rf $S/out` (approved once), (b) the same with the worktree's `scratchpad` a symlink to a user-owned directory outside the job (main), (c) `test -d sub && cd sub; rm -f x` (main), (d) `npm run release` in the worktree (main), (e) `cp a.txt <worktree>/dir/` (main unless the derived child is proven): only (a) gets a key press; the others reach main with recommendation and answer action.
tickets.what: Milestone review j052818360e2b58a8 findings 7-10 and its deletion list, `src/mcp/permission-policy.ts`. Prefer narrowing unsupported forms to main over growing a shell interpreter; spec §2.1 approves only what is proven confined and reversible, anything unsure goes to main. (7) `resolveRoots` (~125-153) realpaths `worktree/scratchpad` and `task/scratchpad` and trusts the destination on a UID match; a symlinked scratchpad makes an outside directory a deletion root. Anchor each derived root beneath its verified job parent (realpath must stay inside it). (8) `tokenizeShell`/`proveShellPrompt` (~322-380, ~1297-1315, ~1350-1359) flatten conditionals and persist assignments/`cd` as if executed; only allow state-bearing sequences (assignment, cd) when every earlier separator is unconditional and not in a pipeline; otherwise main. (9) `validateCpMv` (~643-691) checks the destination directory, not the derived child; `validateTar`/`validateUnzip` (~773-876) do not check extracted members. Prove the effective child target (no existing symlink, recoverable or new) or send to main; tar/unzip without proven member lists go to main. (10) `npm run <script>` and `npx tsc` (~1044-1158) are not evidence of a local-only effect: hand them to main unless a trusted confined route exists (e.g. `npx --no-install tsc` with a local `node_modules/.bin/tsc` inside the worktree); arbitrary script names go to main. Delete the old PNG-only `permissionDirectory`, the root-string `permissionProof` adapter and the string branch of `normalizeProof` (~110, ~1418, ~1431); tests use the structured proof. Update docs/reference.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §5 where the approved set changes; ticket 07's acceptance item that listed `npm run build` as auto-approved is superseded by this narrowing. Verify line numbers at HEAD first.

acceptance.text: Tests: symlinked scratchpad, conditional `cd`/assignment before `;`, `cp` into a directory with an existing child symlink, tar/unzip without member list, `npm run release` and `npx tsc` without a proven local binary all go to main
Tests: `S=<scratchpad>; rm -rf $S/out`, `mkdir -p`/`cp` to explicit new targets inside the worktree and a Claude Edit file inside the worktree are still approved
The legacy string proof path is removed and no test passes a bare string as a verified proof
docs/reference.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describe the narrowed approved set

tickets.what: Owner decision D-2026-11-27-02 after milestone review j297aaffd5e903d3d (run q2e663015e61f3272, cancelled). Delete, do not patch: the proof in `src/mcp/permission-policy.ts` (~1,350 lines) and `src/mcp/worker-permissions.ts` keeps growing into a shell and Git interpreter. Remove these branches so the forms go to main: (1) git `add`/`commit`/`stash`/`rebase` from `ALLOWED_GIT_SUBS` (~:11, ~1043-1133); Git read subcommands accept only known options; (2) recursive chmod/traversal and recursive search, and nonrecursive chmod on multiply-linked files (~762-795, ~934-996); (3) any proof that carries `cd` or assignment state across `;`/`&&` into a mutation (~1186-1188, ~1242-1250), except the literal `S=<abs>; rm ... $S/...` form ticket 08 kept; (4) native edit prompts with a relative heading path: use the displayed cwd when unambiguous, else main; never substitute the process cwd (`worker-permissions.ts` ~126-161, ~360-363); (5) external scratch and temp roots that lack a verified real parent bound to the job (`worker-permissions.ts` ~340-359, `permission-policy.ts` ~116-158): drop them from automatic deletion proof; the derived worktree scratchpad stays. Also: bare shell verbs must resolve to a trusted system path, not a project-local executable (~348-363), or go to main. Keep: the structured-only Decision API input, recoverable-byte check, bounded ledger, spend-before-send, fresh menu/selection check, worktree explicit new-file create/edit, scratchpad deletion, read-only commands with known options and read-only filter pipes. Net line count of the two files must go down. Update docs/reference.md (permission section, ~677-687) and the Decision API input table (~1347) to the narrowed set.

tickets.title: Close the permission-handoff and notice delivery holes from the last unattended review
tickets.what: Review j297aaffd5e903d3d majors 6-10 plus open lead todos (run q2e663015e61f3272, cancelled; its repair budget was spent). Verify line numbers at HEAD. (6) `src/mcp/report-notes.ts` ~159-169 ends an inline field at a same-indent next line, so a soft-wrapped `Blockers: owner live try remains: ...` + `and pick which layout ships` is classified as a try: collect through the Markdown paragraph/field boundary before classifying, or keep ambiguous continuation as a blocker. (7) `src/roles/notify.ts` ~187-209 types the message after any unsuccessful `codex queue` result, including timeout and lost reply (`src/roles/herdr-run.ts`): fall back only on positive non-send evidence; propagate indeterminate. (8) `src/cli/watch.ts` ~67-70, ~470-600 treats a permission notice as a row delta and advances `prev` before delivery, so a confirmed non-send or expired guarded retry loses the hand-off: use one durable per-entry delivery claim shared by watcher and direct paths (`src/runtime/watch-runtime.ts` ~294-324), release only on confirmed non-send, and prune `.noticed` markers with the 12-entry ledger. (9) `src/mcp/ticket-queue-step.ts` ~53, ~73-92, ~1421-1437 disables the project permission outbox because historical `q.pane` is non-empty after the origin died: choose by live recipient availability. (10) `src/mcp/mcp/tasks.ts` ~443-470 prefers the global marker epoch/expiry over the caller's receipt: check the caller's own receipt epoch against the flow before poll/cancel/re-claim. Also: (11) `hud_respond` on run q2e663015e61f3272 paused with `handback {kind: escalate, step: accept}` returned `no_pending_handback` (2026-11-27); an escalate pause must be answerable with resume/stop. (12) Check `judgeSettlement` (`ticket-queue-step.ts` ~148) cannot wait forever when a report is rewritten after settlement; add a bound or a notice.

acceptance.text: Tests for each of items 6-12: soft-wrapped Blockers stays a blocker; an indeterminate codex queue send is not retyped; a refused watcher hand-off is redelivered once and .noticed markers stay bounded; a pane-less successor still notifies project main; a stale caller receipt cannot poll a newer epoch's task; hud_respond answers an escalate accept pause; a rewritten report cannot wait forever
docs/reference.md matches the changed delivery rules

tickets.title: Drop Git from permission auto-approval; keep indented Blockers children
tickets.what:
From milestone review jaf9f426dbdf5c418 (blocker 1 and major 6).

1. Git. `src/mcp/permission-policy.ts` (~972–1008) classifies ordinary `git diff` (and similar Git reads) as `read_only`. Git can run repository-configured helpers (external diff, textconv, fsmonitor, pager and similar) on ordinary read commands, so a system-Git argv check does not prove a read. Remove every Git form from the worker auto-approval set: any `git ...` permission prompt goes to main. Delete the Git-read classifier code rather than adding another Git interpreter. HUD's own internal index check (~288–298) is HUD-run, not a worker prompt, and stays.
2. Blockers parsing. `src/mcp/report-notes.ts` (~164–175) now breaks on every bullet, so `- Blockers: owner live try remains` followed by an indented `  - Owner must choose which layout ships` loses the child. Keep indented child bullets in their enclosing field (a nested item under Blockers is a blocker). The same-indent prose cases added by unattended/26 stay.

This narrows auto-approval further, in line with D-2026-11-27-02 (narrow, then ship). Update the auto-approval list in `docs/reference.md` (and `.zh`) to say Git commands go to main.
Out of scope: notice delivery, receipts and task epochs (reviewer majors 2–5; separate design pass), judgeSettlement cleanup.
Size: net negative source lines in permission-policy; one or two parser tests; adjust existing worker-permissions tests that expected Git auto-approval.

acceptance.text: A worker permission prompt for `git diff`, `git log -p` or `git status` is handed to main, never auto-approved.
No Git-specific read classifier remains in `src/mcp/permission-policy.ts`.
A report with `- Blockers: ...` followed by an indented child bullet records the child as a blocker and the ticket does not land without the owner.
`docs/reference.md` lists Git as going to main.

tickets.title: hud_respond cannot answer Claude prompts with a countdown line
tickets.what:
Observed 2026-11-27 on job jf9d58d8952e4d5c6 (Claude Code worker, unattended session): the permission prompt carries `⚠ Claude Code will automatically block this request in 1:57, to avoid holding up an unattended session`, and the time ticks every second. `hud_respond` with the notice's request_id returned `prompt_changed`; the re-issued request id then returned `option_unavailable`; main had to press Enter through `herdr pane send-keys`. The prompt identity/verification that guards key delivery must ignore this countdown line (treat the line as volatile: strip or normalise the `in M:SS` part before hashing and comparing), while still refusing when the command text, options or selected option change.

Out of scope: other prompt kinds, the delivery-state redesign.
Size: small; one watcher/permission test with a prompt whose countdown changes between capture and delivery.

acceptance.text: A Claude permission prompt whose countdown text changes between notice and answer is still answered by `hud_respond approve` with the notice's request_id, and the key lands.
A prompt whose command text or selected option changed is still refused with `prompt_changed`.

tickets.title: One delivery-state record and call-time recipient lookup for notices and permission hand-offs
tickets.what:
Implement section 1.1–1.3 of oracle design j4b2631efe93fb5fb (read it with `hud_read({job: "j4b2631efe93fb5fb", mode: "full"})`; it is the spec for this ticket), except the MCP task-reload part (next ticket). Main decisions taken from it (main, 2026-11-27): permission routing fork A (one job-level `perm-<id>.noticed` path for every job kind; delete `syncPermissionNotices`), `sending` state fork A.

In short:
- `.noticed`/`.observed` become atomic 0600 JSON records `{v, state, epoch, pid?, start?, via?, reason?, at, expires?}` with states pending (absent) / claimed / sending / accepted / unknown / abandoned; legacy 0-byte files read as accepted; never write 0-byte files. Unknown is never read as delivered nor as not-sent.
- One `resolveRecipient` at call time (origin pane live → origin; else any live main-agent pane of the same project root; listing failure → leave pending). No stored pane routing tables (owner rule: look up panes at call time).
- `hud_respond` on `perm-*` allowed for a project main when the origin pane is gone (`operations.ts` ~925).
- Deletions: `syncPermissionNotices` (`ticket-queue-step.ts` ~75–104); `codexQueueRefusalText` and substring checks in `src/roles/notify.ts` (refusal only on structured codes, ENOENT, pre-exec usage exit 2); the permission branch of `jobChanges` (`thin-jobs.ts` ~526–529) and `verbose && !first ? [] :` in `watch.ts` ~485; `FOREIGN_NOTICED_PRUNE_MS` and bare `existsSync` delivery checks (`events.ts`, `watch-runtime.ts` ~240). Antigravity stop: commit `sent.accepted` claims before releasing the rest.
- Update `docs/reference.md` (and `.zh`) where delivery/permission routing is described.
Out of scope: MCP `flowTasks` reload authority (next ticket), the oracle's unrequested hardening list, permission classification (unattended/27).
Size: oracle estimate ~+175/−140 source lines over ~9 files, ~150 test lines in existing suites. Stop and report if it grows past ~1.5×.

acceptance.text: A worker started before its main pane exits hits a permission prompt: another live main pane in the same project receives the approve/decline notice and can answer it with `hud_respond`; `syncPermissionNotices` no longer exists.
`codex queue` exit 1 with stderr containing `permission denied` or `no such file` is treated as unknown and the notice is not typed again.
`hud watch --verbose` emits a post-startup permission once and nothing for it after a restart while it is still blocked.
Stopping an Antigravity queue watch after the mailbox accepted an item keeps that item accepted and releases only the unaccepted ones.
A flake-block index entry is pruned only on accepted delivery or a missing/landed source, never while a claim is in flight; no 60 s foreign-claim timer remains.

tickets.title: MCP task reload keeps only receipts this process owns
tickets.what:
Finding 5 of review jaf9f426dbdf5c418, designed in oracle report j4b2631efe93fb5fb §1.3 (read it with `hud_read`). On hot reload, `src/mcp/mcp/server.ts` ~320–330 rebuilds a missing flow-task caller receipt from `landTasks: Set<string>` using `flow.epoch` and `created_at + TASK_TTL`, which `tasks.ts` then accepts, including for cancel. Replace `landTasks` with `flowTasks: Map<id, {id, epoch?, expiresAt}>` in `snapshot()`; delete the fabrication. Legacy Set entries (one upgrade reload) backfill only from an unexpired queue task marker matching this process's pid, start time and the flow epoch; otherwise the task is unknown. `tasks/get` and `tasks/cancel` on an unknown task answer `unknownTask` (point to `hud_read`); cancel additionally needs in-memory connection authority.
Out of scope: notice/permission delivery records (other ticket), the oracle's unrequested hardening list.
Size: ~+35/−25 source lines in server.ts, tasks.ts, task-bounds.ts, operations.ts; one reload unit test.

acceptance.text: After `snapshot()` → reload with a missing caller receipt and a foreign or absent `flows/<q>/task.json`, both `tasks/get` and `tasks/cancel` report the task unknown and nothing is cancelled.
A task this process owns survives a reload with the same epoch and expiry.
